from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Most sphere volume migrates to the shell.",
            "The center becomes hollow as dimensions grow.",
            "Think of an orange with a giant peel.",
            "Almost all mass concentrates near the crust.",

        ]
        self.setup_layout("The 'Empty' Core Paradox", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create visual elements

        self.place_at_grid(sphere_core, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # 2. Formalization
        integral_text = MathTex(r"V_{shell} = \int_{r-\epsilon}^{r} S_n(r')dr'", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(integral_text, 'C5', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # 3. Visual Synthesis (Shell highlight)
        shell = Annulus(inner_radius=1.0, outer_radius=1.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(shell, 'E3', scale_factor=0.5)

        # 4. Analogy (Orange)
        orange = Circle(radius=1.5, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.2)
        peel = Annulus(inner_radius=1.3, outer_radius=1.5, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=1.0)
        orange_group = VGroup(orange, peel)
        self.place_at_grid(orange_group, 'E5', scale_factor=0.5)

        # 5. Summary (99%)
        percent_label = Text("99% volume", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(percent_label, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)

        # Animations with color changes (Mandatory Constraint)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF69B4"), sphere_core.animate.set_color("#FF69B4"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#32CD32"), shell.animate.set_color("#32CD32"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), percent_label.animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application & Summary", [
            "Data science uses distance for classification.",
            "Hyperspheres cluster similar user preferences efficiently.",
            "High-dimensional spaces defy our 3D intuition."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Prerequisites: Show a scatter plot of high-dimensional points.
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color=BLUE) for _ in range(20)])
        dots.arrange_in_grid(4, 5, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(dots, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(dots), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF69B4"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Formalization: Display the KNN search formula.
        formula = MathTex(r"d(x, y) = \sqrt{\sum (x_i - y_i)^2}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Real-world: Animate a search engine clustering points.
        circle = Circle(radius=1.0, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'F3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(circle), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Introduction: Beyond 3D Intuition (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Define the n-dimensional sphere (hypersphere) using the equation Σxᵢ² = R². Contrast the 2D circle and 3D sphere to prime the audience for abstraction.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'slicing' animation where a 3D sphere passes through a 2D plane (becoming a circle), helping students visualize a 4D sphere passing through 3D space.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Distance Formula (0:45-1:30)
sections.content: Briefly revisit the Pythagorean theorem and Euclidean distance. Establish that distance in n-dimensions is simply an extension: d = √(x₁² + x₂² + ... + xₙ²).
sections.example: A 2D character (Dotty) calculating the distance to a point, then extending the formula to a 3D character (Cube) moving in a room.

sections.title: The 'Empty' Core Paradox (1:30-2:45)
sections.content: Discuss the distribution of volume. As dimensions increase, volume migrates from the center to the 'crust' of the sphere. Mathematically show that for very high dimensions, almost all volume lies within an infinitesimally thin shell near the surface.
sections.example: An orange analogy: As the 'orange' (hypersphere) grows in dimension, the 'peel' (the surface region) holds 99% of the fruit, leaving the center virtually empty.

sections.title: The Corner Concentration Mystery (2:45-4:15)
sections.content: Explain that hyperspheres inscribed in a hypercube barely touch the sides, and the 'corners' of the cube become increasingly vast. This explains why high-dimensional data points are often sparse.
sections.example: A robot trying to navigate a high-dimensional box; it finds that the 'corners' are so far away that it essentially gets lost in the voids, while the sphere stays central.

sections.title: Real-World Application & Summary (4:15-5:00)
sections.content: Connect high-dimensional spheres to Data Science (k-Nearest Neighbors) and Machine Learning, where 'distances' behave counter-intuitively in high-dimensional feature spaces.
sections.example: A search engine algorithm that views each query as a point in a 10,000-dimensional space, using hyperspheres to cluster similar user preferences.
